qt: to the Commission Lefteris Nikolaou-Alavanos (NI) Subject:

Greece and Europe have been witnessing an explosive rise in energy costs, due to the continuation of imperialist wars and the involvement of the EU and Member State governments. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What is its take on the fact that the EU’s guidelines on energy liberalisation, the ‘green’ transition, the lignite phase-out and subsidies from every manner of funds and programmes (Repower EU, Accelerate EU, Social Climate Fund, Island Decarbonisation Fund, etc.) have not brought down electricity and fuel prices, as the EU has claimed, but on the contrary, the achievement of ‘green’ targets has proven to be linked with a surge in prices for the working classes and record profits for energy groups?

What is its take on the fact that EU governments’ compliance with budgetary discipline and surpluses achieved through brutal sacrifices in order to service public debt created not by the people but by monopolies, means keeping VAT and excise duties, massively pushing up the price of energy and fuel, while the Commission issues new outrageous requests to the people to ‘reduce consumption’ by suppressing their needs, with any reductions in tax rates being temporary in nature and involving, as in Spain’s case, tax reductions shifting from petrol to diesel and vice versa, subsidising and perpetuating the system of high prices?
